spec.title: Flow: Codkit seam catalogue of the theia type

p.PROJECT-HAS-A-SEAM-CATALOGUE: This repository is a patch set of the **theia** project type, and the catalogue of the seams its upstream family offers — the ways an Eclipse Theia monorepo itself lets a product add or change behaviour, ranked from a pull request upstream down to the internals of a module — is @spec://org.vibevm.codkit/seams-theia/flows/standards/seam-catalogue#root. The universal standard of minimal intervention is a separate package and is cited from its own snippet.

p.THE-CATALOGUE-IS-A-MENU: The catalogue is a menu, never this product's seam map: the map is the product's own instance, dated to its pin, naming its own interventions, and it lives in the product's specs (`MI-SEAM-MAP-REQUIRED` of the standard).

p.A-TYPE-OWNS-ITS-SEAMS: A patch set carries the seam catalogue of its own project type and no other: the tiers, the seams and the example locations here are facts about this family of upstreams, and a patch set of another type is delivered another catalogue or none at all.

p.THE-HIGHEST-TIERS-COST-NOTHING: In this family the two highest tiers of the catalogue reach further than in most: an addition needs **no upstream edit at all** — own code is a workspace package, it enters an application by one line of that application's own `package.json`, and a service is replaced by an inversify `rebind` in the own container module. A patch of an upstream file is therefore an unusual event here, and the seam map has to say what forced it.
